Expect to reconstruct tooling before the project's own test command will run, and say so in your report: the cost of that reconstruction is the evidence that this project should declare `worktree_setup`.\n  **Your environment is inherited, not isolated.** A worktree isolates *files*; the process that spawned you hands down its *environment* unchanged. `VIRTUAL_ENV`, `PATH` and their per-ecosystem equivalents can still point into the checkout you were sent away from, so a bare `python`, `pytest` or `npm` may run another tree's tooling against another tree's source while reporting cleanly. Two consequences, and the second is the dangerous one: a result you believe is about your worktree can be about someone else's, and an installer that honours an inherited `VIRTUAL_ENV` will install *your* unmerged source into *their* environment — a corruption that points away from you, that your own tests cannot see, and that reports success on both sides. Check what you are actually running (`command -v python`, or import the package and print its `__file__`) before you trust a green, prefer in-tree absolute paths over whatever `PATH` resolves, and set the environment explicitly for any installer that reads it.\n\n## Record summary\n\n(no description)\n\n**Status**: open\n**Plan membership**: (none)\n\n## Criteria\n\n| id | text | state | reason (if void/unobserved) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| TST-1.c1 | the CLI is wired | unmet-unbuilt |  |\n\n1 live criteria · 0 void (none withheld from this table)\n\n\n## Touches\n\n| declared by | path | symbol |\n|---|---|---|\n| TST-1 (this dispatch's own record) | src/app.py | (whole file) |\n\nThis is also the set `kyo dispatch` checked for disjointness against every other running dispatch, so it is both what you were checked against and what you may change (KYO-76). read a test run's failures only** (enforced-by: aspirational)\n  Issue independent reads, searches, and status commands together in one turn instead of one per turn, and run any test quietly, with its output sent to a file, reading back only its failures — a turn re-reads your whole context, and printed output is re-read on every turn after it is printed.\n- **Keep every foreground command under about four minutes** (enforced-by: aspirational)\n  Keep any single foreground command under about four minutes, and before you hand back, end or stop every background task you started -- monitors included, since stopping the run one watches does not stop the watcher.\n- **Spawn helpers read-only if at all, and own everything they do** (enforced-by: aspirational, with one mechanical edge — `kyo check-clean --subagent-stop`, `src/kyosei/cmd_guard.py` (in Kyosei's own repository))\n  You may spawn helper subagents, and one read-only helper that surveys a file set and reports back is often the cheapest way to answer a question your brief needs answered.\n- **Read each governed section your branch raises, and propose its verdict in `docs_verdicts[]`** (enforced-by: mechanism, partial — `kyo report`, `kyo docs settle --from-report <dispatch-id>`)\n  Most docs obligations settle `not-affected`: in measured consumer stores they outnumber `updated` by between two and nine to one, and a single dispatch can raise sixty at once.\n\nEach rule above is its title, its one-line enforced-by (the level, and the commands or tests that hold it up), and the first sentence of the ledger's reasoning — the ledger's own words, never a paraphrase. Run the tests that cover your change and leave the whole suite to your orchestrator: a suite that holds an exclusive resource — a port, a display, a database, a device — manufactures failures when two runs fight over it, and even where it holds none, your green would be on this branch before every other worker's merge, which is not the question anyone needs answered.\n- **Worktree tooling**: this project declares none (`worktree_setup` is unset in `kyosei/config.yml`), so nothing was provisioned for you and this brief promises nothing about what is installed. Your worktree was created by `git worktree add`, which checks out **tracked files only**: every gitignored dependency and build artifact — a `.venv/`, a `node_modules/`, a compiled binary, a seeded database — is absent, no matter what the project's README, CLAUDE.md or Makefile say, because those describe a checkout somebody had already built in. Expect to reconstruct tooling before the project's own test command will run, and say so in your report: the cost of that reconstruction is the evidence that this project should declare `worktree_setup`.\n  **Your environment is inherited, not isolated.** A worktree isolates *files*; the process that spawned you hands down its *environment* unchanged. `VIRTUAL_ENV`, `PATH` and their per-ecosystem equivalents can still point into the checkout you were sent away from, so a bare `python`, `pytest` or `npm` may run another tree's tooling against another tree's source while reporting cleanly. Two consequences, and the second is the dangerous one: a result you believe is about your worktree can be about someone else's, and an installer that honours an inherited `VIRTUAL_ENV` will install *your* unmerged source into *their* environment — a corruption that points away from you, that your own tests cannot see, and that reports success on both sides. Check what you are actually running (`command -v python`, or import the package and print its `__file__`) before you trust a green, prefer in-tree absolute paths over whatever `PATH` resolves, and set the environment explicitly for any installer that reads it.\n\n## Record summary\n\n(no description)\n\n**Status**: open\n**Plan membership**: (none)\n\n## Criteria\n\n| id | text | state | reason (if void/unobserved) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| TST-1.c1 | the CLI is wired | unmet-unbuilt |  |\n\n1 live criteria · 0 void (none withheld from this table)\n\n\n## Touches\n\n| declared by | path | symbol |\n|---|---|---|\n| TST-1 (this dispatch's own record) | src/app.py | (whole file) |\n\nThis is also the set `kyo dispatch` checked for disjointness against every other running dispatch, so it is both what you were checked against and what you may change (KYO-76). do not park on a stop signal with a dirty worktree** (enforced-by: `SubagentStop` hook, `kyo check-clean`)\n  A worker that finishes with unstaged or uncommitted work and then stops is one crash away from losing it — `git log main..HEAD` reads empty in that state, which looks identical to \"nothing was done.\" Commit continuously as you complete units of work, not once at the end.\n- **Flag conflicts with the brief; do not silently resolve them yourself** (enforced-by: mechanism, partial — `kyo report-schema`, `kyo report`)\n  If a premise in your brief is false, or you disagree with the approach you were told to take, say so structurally — do not quietly do what you think is right instead, and do not quietly comply with something you believe is wrong.\n- **Stay inside the dispatch's `write_scope`** (enforced-by: aspirational in v1)\n  `write_scope` (`none | queries-only | code | prod-data`) is a mechanical capability statement, not a suggestion.\n- **Never write to the structured store directly** (enforced-by: mechanism, partial — `kyo check-branch`, `src/kyosei/cmd_guard.py` (in Kyosei's own repository))\n  You cannot move a record, check a criterion, or edit `kinds.yml`/`procedures.md` from a dispatch.\n- **Never state a timestamp, line count, or other tool-derivable fact from memory** (enforced-by: aspirational)\n  Run `kyo show --json`, `kyo brief`, `wc -l`, or `date` at the moment you need the fact, and cite what it returned.\n- **Write a long run to a file and read the file; never pipe a suite through `tail`** (enforced-by: aspirational — `make test LOG=<file>`, `tests/test_kyo193_logged_runs.py` (in Kyosei's own repository))\n  Run `cmd > file 2>&1; echo \"exit=$?\"` and then read the file — or a project target that does exactly that.\n- **Never deploy, and never mutate a production system outside the declared `write_scope`** (enforced-by: mechanism, partial)\n  Deciding a change is fit to ship, and shipping it, is a judgment made with the whole project in view — which a dispatched worker does not have.\n- **Run the tests that cover your change, not the whole suite** (enforced-by: mechanism, partial — `kyo dispatch`, `tests/test_procedures.py` (in Kyosei's own repository))\n  Run the tests that cover what you changed, and leave the whole suite to your orchestrator.\n- **Batch independent calls into one turn; read a test run's failures only** (enforced-by: aspirational)\n  Issue independent reads, searches, and status commands together in one turn instead of one per turn, and run any test quietly, with its output sent to a file, reading back only its failures — a turn re-reads your whole context, and printed output is re-read on every turn after it is printed.\n- **Keep every foreground command under about four minutes** (enforced-by: aspirational)\n  Keep any single foreground command under about four minutes, and before you hand back, end or stop every background task you started -- monitors included, since stopping the run one watches does not stop the watcher.\n- **Spawn helpers read-only if at all, and own everything they do** (enforced-by: aspirational, with one mechanical edge — `kyo check-clean --subagent-stop`, `src/kyosei/cmd_guard.py` (in Kyosei's own repository))\n  You may spawn helper subagents, and one read-only helper that surveys a file set and reports back is often the cheapest way to answer a question your brief needs answered.\n- **Read each governed section your branch raises, and propose its verdict in `docs_verdicts[]`** (enforced-by: mechanism, partial — `kyo report`, `kyo docs settle --from-report <dispatch-id>`)\n  Most docs obligations settle `not-affected`: in measured consumer stores they outnumber `updated` by between two and nine to one, and a single dispatch can raise sixty at once.\n\nEach rule above is its title, its one-line enforced-by (the level, and the commands or tests that hold it up), and the first sentence of the ledger's reasoning — the ledger's own words, never a paraphrase. The rest of each rule (the whole enforced-by argument, the incident behind it, what it admits it does NOT cover) is one read-only command away: `kyo rules \"<title>\"` prints one rule verbatim, and `kyo rules` alone lists every rule this project carries. Read the full text of any rule you are about to lean on (KYO-327).\n\n## Standing stance\n\n**Flag conflicts, do not resolve them. Commit your work before you stop; an uncommitted worktree at stop time is checked and blocked. **Do not commit the report itself**: `.kyosei-report.json` is gitignored in this project, `kyo check-clean` does not count it as uncommitted work, and `kyo touch-drift` never names it — it is your output, which `kyo report` ingests and the store keeps, not a file your branch should carry.\n\nKeep your final message to a few lines: the dispatch id, that the report is written, the branch tip sha, and only what the report cannot carry — say why in one clause: the report is structured and is about to be read.\n\nBefore you hand back, run `kyo report TST-1.d1 --file .kyosei-report.json --check` in your worktree: it runs every check the ingest runs before it writes (the schema, the ids, criteria scoping, your commits on the declared branch), prints any problem, and writes nothing.
